extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel, patent practitioners, applicants, and members of the public seeking access to patent application information
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria under 37 CFR 1.11 and 1.14 (MPEP §103) governing when and how patent application files or status information may be disclosed to the public, including IFW, published/unpublished, international filings, petitions for access, and incorporation-by-reference issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of unpublished applications (37 CFR 1.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a); information concerning filing, pendency, subject matter, status information, and access will only be given to the public as set forth in § 1.11 or in § 1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline rule: unpublished applications are presumptively confidential. Any exception must be authorized by the specified regulatory provisions (e.g., publication, identification, benefit claims, petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible status information (definition and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Status information of an application means only the following information: (A) whether the application is pending, abandoned, or patented; (B) whether the application has been published; (C) the application number or the serial number plus any one of the filing date of the national application, the international filing date, or the date of entry into the national stage; and (D) whether another application claims the benefit of the application and corresponding status information for that application (per 37 CFR 1.14(a)(2) and related text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only these enumerated items may be communicated to the public even where an application is identified; other continuity data (e.g., whether application is CIP/continuation/divisional, abandonment date, issue date) may remain confidential unless specifically authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may receive status information without petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Status information may be given to authorized requesters when the requester is: (1) the applicant; (2) a patent practitioner of record; (3) the assignee or an assignee of an undivided part interest; (4) the inventor or a joint inventor; or (5) a registered attorney or agent named in the papers accompanying the application (with nuance about power of attorney per 37 CFR 1.32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requester falls into (1)-(5) or has written authority signed by one of them, the requester is entitled to status information. Otherwise, requesters should use Patent Center or may be directed to AAU for pre-/post-examination help. See MPEP §104 for written-authority details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Image File Wrapper (IFW) files
rubrics_metrics.description: For IFW applications the IFW file is the Official file; paper documents used to create the IFW are not accessible. IFW files (except certain non-patent literature) are accessible through Patent Center once scanned/created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All processing and examination is done using electronic images; for IFW-maintained applications, the IFW is the official record and paper source sheets are not available. Most applications filed after June 30, 2003 are in IFW and therefore accessible via Patent Center upon publication or patenting (subject to confidentiality rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to published applications and patents (37 CFR 1.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, drawings, and all papers relating to the file of a published application, a patent, or a statutory invention registration are open to inspection by the public; copies may be obtained upon payment of the fee set forth in § 1.19(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a redacted copy was used for publication under § 1.217, a complete file may not be available while the application is still pending; redacted materials limit what is provided. Published IFW-maintained applications are available through Patent Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to published abandoned and published pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The file of an abandoned published application is available to the public under § 1.11(a). A copy of the application-as-filed, the file contents of a pending published application, or a specific document therein may be provided upon written request and payment of the fee (§ 1.19(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication used a redacted copy, the copy provided will be the redacted version. The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a published pending application except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i) of § 1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to unpublished abandoned applications that are identified or relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: File contents of an unpublished, abandoned application may be made available if the application is identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, published international application (PCT Art. 21(2)), or publication of an international registration (Hague Art. 10(3)); or if benefit of the abandoned application is claimed in an application that has issued or published as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification requires explicit identification in the printed patent/publication text (application number/serial number, filing date, first named inventor, title, etc.). Identification only in a paper in the file contents but not in the printed patent is insufficient. Access requires a written request and payment of § 1.19(b) fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to unpublished pending applications whose benefit is claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the file contents of an unpublished pending application may be provided upon written request and payment of the fee if the benefit of the application is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) in an application that has issued as a U.S. patent or has published as a statutory invention registration or application publication (per 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the application-as-filed or a specific document in the pending application's file may also be provided under the same conditions. The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraphs (c) or (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to unpublished pending applications incorporated by reference or otherwise identified
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application-as-filed of an unpublished pending application may be provided upon written request and payment if the application is incorporated by reference or otherwise identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, published international application (PCT Art. 21(2)), or publication of an international registration designating the U.S. (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i). Incorporation-by-reference must appear in the printed publication/patent text (not only in a paper in the file) to trigger this access.

rubrics_metrics.name: When petition for access or power to inspect is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that were not published or patented, that are not subject of a benefit claim, and that are not identified in authorized publications are not available to the public; if such an application is identified only within file contents of another application (but not in the published patent/publication), a granted petition for access or a power to inspect is necessary to obtain the application or a copy (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(vii) and (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identification is incomplete (e.g., only in file contents), public access is blocked absent a petition or power to inspect; similarly wholly-unpublished/unidentified applications require petition with showing of necessity or special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for access requirements and standards (37 CFR 1.14(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition by a member of the public seeking access to, or copies of, all or part of any pending or abandoned application preserved in confidence must include: (1) the fee set forth in § 1.17(g); and (2) a showing that access is necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or that special circumstances exist which warrant access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be filed to the Director (Office of Patent Legal Administration handles most petitions). The petition should include full post office address (ZIP) and contact info; may be filed with proof of service on applicant/inventor/assignee/attorney (or in duplicate for Office to serve applicant). A separate petition (and fee) is required for each application file sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-initiated or special-circumstance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may, sua sponte or on petition, provide access or copies of all or part of an application if necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or if warranted by other special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides discretion to the Office beyond the enumerated access categories, but requires the statutory/administrative justification (Act of Congress or special circumstances) and appropriate petition showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-reference: full vs partial and waiver consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference of a pending application in a U.S. patent application publication or U.S. patent permits a member of the public to obtain a copy of the application-as-filed without petition. However, partial incorporation (only part of an application) is a 'special circumstance' and requires a petition for access to the incorporated material; incorporation-by-reference waives confidentiality only for the incorporated part, not the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant objects to access to the entire application file after incorporation-by-reference, applicant must file two copies of the information incorporated by reference along with the objection; failure to provide the material within the time provided results in the incorporated material (including prosecution history) being made available. Office will not attempt to separate noted materials from the remainder of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to international and national-stage applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a national stage application or claims the benefit of a published international application where the U.S. was indicated as a Designated State, the requester is entitled to status information for the national stage application and any applications claiming benefit; a copy of the first page of the published international application or corresponding PCT Gazette page must be supplied with the status request (37 CFR 1.14(a)(2)(iv) and related text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only limited status information (serial number/filing date and pending/abandoned/patented) may be given for national-stage and related applications; other continuity data on the continuity data screen (e.g., CIP/continuation/divisional, abandonment date, issue date) may be confidential and should not be communicated. Requests for national-stage status should be made in writing to International Patent Legal Administration or PCT Help desk as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcements and availability for reissue and reexamination matters
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications and all requests for reexamination satisfying §§ 1.510/1.915 will be announced in the Official Gazette and the announcement must include at least filing date, reissue application and original patent numbers, title, class/subclass, inventor, owner of record, attorney/agent of record, and examining group. Papers entered of record in reexamination proceedings are open to inspection and copies furnished upon payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexaminations initiated by the Director under § 1.520 are also announced. This creates public availability of certain reissue/reexamination documents and basic metadata in the Official Gazette; full papers may be obtained for a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to interference or PTAB trial files
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as prohibited in § 41.6(b), § 42.14, or § 42.410(b), the file of any interference or trial before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board is open to public inspection and copies may be obtained upon payment of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain statutory/regulatory prohibitions may limit access; otherwise PTAB files are generally public and copyable for a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain copies and acceptable payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of a patent application-as-filed and the contents of a patent application file wrapper may be ordered online or requested by facsimile from the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch (Certified Copy Center). Payment of the appropriate fee under 37 CFR 1.19(b) may be made by USPTO Deposit Account, American Express, Discover, MasterCard, or Visa by any person having a right to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access; abandoned applications meeting § 1.14(a)(1)(iv) and certain file wrapper continuation items are available through the Certified Copy Center. Non-U.S. applications are not accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on providing paper file for pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application that has been published, and will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i) of § 1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when copies of electronic contents are available, physical paper source files are generally not provided for pending applications—access is by copy or electronic IFW, unless specific exceptions apply.
